heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Eryone Silk PLA out of the box with exceptional surface finish, constrained to a safe max print speed of 143 mm/s due to its 12 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. While the hardened steel nozzle is standard on the X1C, ensure the top glass or front door is vented to prevent heat creep during prolonged prints.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate or Smooth PEI Plate with no adhesive required (clean with dish soap and warm water)
slicerTweaks: Cap the Maximum Volumetric Speed to 12 mm³/s in the Eryone Silk PLA filament profile to prevent matte patches and under-extrusion.
Set outer wall speed to a uniform 60-80 mm/s to ensure consistent silk sheen and avoid directional reflectivity banding.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' with a 2 mm wipe distance to eliminate surface stringing and zits inherent to low-viscosity silk additives.
Keep the chamber vented by popping open the top glass cover or leaving the front door ajar to maintain chamber temperatures below 35°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Inconsistent sheen with alternating glossy and matte bands
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Fluctuations in print speed and nozzle temperature causing uneven crystallization and melting of elastomers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Normalize Outer Wall and Inner Wall speeds to 80 mm/s and fix nozzle temperature to 215°C across all feature types.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clogs or clicking during long prints
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Chamber heat creep in the enclosed X1C causing the low-Tg silk filament to soften prematurely in the extruder gears.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Prop the top glass lid open with a riser or crack the front door open, keeping the bed temp capped at 60°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak layer adhesion and brittle parts along Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Silk elastomers disrupting interlayer polymer bonding when printed too cold or overcooled by auxiliary fans.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature to 220°C-225°C and reduce Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan speed to 0% in OrcaSlicer.

faq.question: Can I print Eryone Silk PLA at default Bambu standard speeds (250-300 mm/s)?
faq.answer: No, standard Bambu profiles exceed the melt capability of silk polymers; you must cap volumetric flow at 12 mm³/s, yielding a safe maximum print speed of around 143 mm/s.

faq.question: Do I need glue stick on the Bambu Textured PEI plate for Silk PLA?
faq.answer: No, Silk PLA adheres well directly to clean textured PEI at 60°C and releases easily once the plate cools down below 35°C.

faq.question: Why does my silk print look matte instead of shiny?
faq.answer: Silk additives need sufficient heat and lower speeds to orient properly; printing too fast or at too low a temperature causes a dull, matte appearance.

faq.question: Is Eryone Silk PLA compatible with the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, standard 1kg Eryone spools are AMS compatible, but ensure the spool rim is intact (use spool rings if plastic/cardboard rims slip).
